findings.title: Working-hours check computes the slot end from `slotStartTime`
findings.description: In the new working-hours block of `checkIfIsAvailable`, `end` is built from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so it is identical to `start`. It should use `slotEndTime`. As written, the `end > workingHour.endTime` half of the condition can never be true, so slots that run past the end of working hours are treated as available.

findings.title: Comparing two dayjs objects with `===` is always false
findings.description: Inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback, `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The zero-length override early return never fires. Use `.isSame(...)` instead.

findings.title: Working-hours `find` marks a slot unavailable when any single entry excludes it
findings.description: The `workingHours.find(...)` callback returns `true` (and then the function returns `false`) whenever one matching-day entry has `start < startTime || end > endTime`. With several working-hour ranges on the same weekday, a slot inside range B is rejected because it falls outside range A. The condition needs to check whether the slot is inside at least one range, e.g. `!workingHours.some(...)`, rather than rejecting on the first non-containing entry.

findings.title: `toString()` round-trip before `dayjs` parsing is fragile
findings.description: In the `activeOverrides.flatMap` callback, `dayjs(override.start.toString())` converts a `Date` to its locale-formatted string and parses it back. That string format is implementation-dependent and drops milliseconds. Parse the `Date` directly (`dayjs(override.start)`), as the rest of the same callback already does.
